Could this be back ported to 1.26?
It's not clear to me that this should be backported

The issue is that older clusters that have configured node affinity of a PV with the now deprecated labels fails to schedule pods to any node as the cloud controller manager no longer maintains those deprecated labels on the nodes.

One example is with the Azure Cloud Controller Manager which starting from v1.26 no longer maintain the deprecated labels, for example failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone, on the cluster nodes. Effectively, pods mounting such PVs cannot be scheduled to any node as the PVs node affinity cannot be satisfied by any node. And as the node affinity term in the PV is immutable, cluster administrators cannot re-configure the PV to use the new stable label topology.kubernetes.io/zone.

To get out of this deadlock, it would be nice even for older k8s versions the labels keys to be made mutable and this is why I opened the cherry-picks.
I second @vpnachev. We also have reports from customers in the field that the current situation leads to deadlocks in AKS. I assume similar situations are possible in other KE services.
I haven't checked all the cloud controllers yet, but it seems like a problem for those controllers to drop setting the beta labels before kubelet does

It is indeed a problem triggered by cloud controllers removing a bit too early these labels, however they can also argue that it should be safe for labels deprecated 9 minor releases earlier (in k8s v1.17).

Anyway, it is k8s that deprecated those labels and enforces immutability over the PersistentVolume spec, so I think k8s also must allow the users to migrate away from the deprecated labels and it does not sound quite right this to be allowed just in k8s version `>= v1.27`.

issue_context.title: Allow PV NodeAffinity to update from beta to GA topology labels
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114268, we realized that non in-tree PVs can be impacted by a future removal of beta topology labels from Nodes if they are supporting the beta topology labels.

### What did you expect to happen?

We should allow users to mutate the PV NodeAffinity to update uses of the beta topology label to the GA label.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Remove beta topology label from a Node, and try to schedule a Pod using a non-migratable PVC with beta topology label in the PV.NodeAffinity.

Do we allow users to mutate both non in-tree PVs and in-tree PVs, or only non in-tree PVs?

review_comments: I like this approach, a more elegant way to compare part of objects.

Unfortunately I think we want to only allow  updates from
- `failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone`  to `topology.kubernetes.io/zone`
- `failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region` to `topology.kubernetes.io/region`

Generically allowing the labels to change where the label equivalence is not well-defined could introduce unrecoverable race conditions: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/69528#issuecomment-606972452
(maybe allow the beta os/arch labels → GA os/arch labels as well)

Okay, let me confirm, we only allow label updates from:
- `failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone` to `topology.kubernetes.io/zone`
- `failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region` to `topology.kubernetes.io/region`
- `beta.kubernetes.io/arch` to `kubernetes.io/arch`
- `beta.kubernetes.io/os` to `kubernetes.io/os`
- `beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type` to `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type`
Yup that looks good to me.
Can you also add some test cases for multiple terms and expressions with same or different lengths, upgrading a partial set of terms, etc.
